covers: The Intel 8255 programmable peripheral interface as a chip

left_out.why: a derived class with the same four registers and handlers; it forces port B to input and port C to output and keeps the output latches on a mode set

entries.name: Intel 8255 PPI
entries.description: Programmable peripheral interface: three 8-bit ports A, B and C that a mode word sets as inputs, outputs or handshaked ports.
entries.behaviour: Four registers by the low two address bits: port A, port B, port C and the control word. Group A is port A with PC4 to PC7 and group B is port B with PC0 to PC3; group A runs mode 0, 1 or 2 and group B mode 0 or 1. A reset is a mode set of 0x9B.

handlers.pa_r: port A level read: output latch, or 0xFF when port A is an input
handlers.acka_r: port A level read that also pulses PC6 low then high as an acknowledge
handlers.pb_r: port B level read: output latch, or 0xFF when port B is an input
handlers.ackb_r: port B level read that also pulses PC2 low then high as an acknowledge
handlers.pc2_w: PC2 line in: port B strobe or acknowledge in group B mode 1
handlers.pc4_w: PC4 line in: port A strobe in group A mode 1 input or mode 2
handlers.pc6_w: PC6 line in: port A acknowledge in group A mode 1 output or mode 2
